subject: sociology
title: Beliefs & Secularisation: Global Perspective
welcome_lead: Globally, religion isn't dying — Europe is the exception.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology secularisation global perspective US Pentecostalism Norris Inglehart.
final_note: Europe secularises; much of the world doesn't.

concepts.def: Fastest-growing Christianity — Latin America, Africa, Asia.
Religion thrives where life is insecure (Norris & Inglehart).
Many faiths coexist; choice may stimulate religion.
Religion regains public significance — disputed in West, clear elsewhere.
Migrant communities sustain religious practice in host country.

walkthroughs.body_html: 2020 Pew estimates: 84% of world's 7.8bn people identify with a religion. Pentecostalism growing fast: ~280 million adherents, ~25 million yearly converts. Sub-Saharan Africa Christian population grew from 100m (1970) to over 700m today.

The US modernised yet stayed religious — ~65% claim religion important vs ~25% in UK (Pew 2018). Explanations: religious market (Stark), historical immigration, civil religion (Bellah). But: 'nones' rising — 28% of US adults unaffiliated in 2021 vs 16% in 2007.

Norris & Inglehart (2004) 'Sacred and Secular': religious decline correlates with welfare, education and life expectancy. Religion remains strong where these are weak. Secularisation is real but uneven — explained by security, not just modernity.
